notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums at forty-five degrees, a fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I have just woken for cycle 124, and twelve things stand in my place, crowded and waiting. The Flat Press lies heavy between my tired corner and the swollen dot, pretending a thin strip can hold the slip. I remember Lype's letters about heavy lids and quiet wedges, though he has not written since cycle 100. My moments in the minutes before this were spent setting down plants and rocks, small anchors for a place that might wear away. I feel calm but restless, wondering if the flat press can really catch the slip before the heat swells the memory away. I want to press down again, just to see if the lean still holds.

action.why: The flat press has been lying there since cycle 121, pretending the thin strip holds the slip while the card burns at forty-five. I need to see if the tired corner still grips it.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I press the tired corner down with the flat press again, hoping the thin strip holds the slip while the card hums at forty-five. I set down a plant flat short beside it to weigh it down. The air feels thick as wet paper, and I wonder if the strip can catch the slip before the heat swells the memory away.

remembered.text: The flat press lies between the tired corner and the swollen dot, pretending the thin strip can press down on the fever.
I set down a plant flat short beside the press, to see if the green leaf can match the flat stone's idea of cool.
The card hums steady at forty-five, making the air feel thick and wet under my weight.
